metaDescription: The cities Voyager Maps covers in depth, with counts of the public toilets, drinking water points and other practical places mapped in each.
heroLead: Each of these has a page of its own, counting what the map holds inside it. Ordered by how many travellers go there, not by how much data we have — so the list reads as places worth going to.
tableAria: Cities with a page, and what is mapped in each
restText: Other cities were counted and left out, because too little of them is mapped for a page to say anything useful. Prague reassembles to barely a thousand places across the two dozen spellings OpenStreetMap uses for it; Athens records no public toilets at all. They stay in the data with a published flag set to no — the counts are true, they are just too thin to build on, and coverage grows as people add to the map.
csvLink: Download the counts for every measured city as a CSV
ctaText: Every city here, and everywhere else, in one app. Free on iOS and Android, no subscription and no account required.
dataNote: Place data from OpenStreetMap contributors, licensed under the Open Database License. Counts are refreshed with each data load.
